prompt: State what is meant by an isolated system in the context of the principle of conservation of momentum.
hints: What external influence must be absent from the system?
solution: An isolated system is a system upon which no resultant external force acts.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Identify that external forces (e.g. net friction, external pushes) change system momentum.
Step 2: Define isolated system as one where resultant external force is zero.

mark_scheme.criterion: A system on which no resultant external force acts (accept: net external force is zero)
